title: Strings and f-strings
content:
What problem does this solve?
A string is a piece of text. You often need to build readable messages that mix that text with live values — a status line, battle log, or inventory note.

Basic syntax
  f"Health: {health}"

What actually happens
An f-string is a string with f before the opening quote. At runtime Python finds each {expression}, evaluates it, converts the result to text, and inserts it into the surrounding string.

Last lesson you printed values separately, or used print("HP:", health) with two arguments. An f-string keeps the whole sentence in one template: f"HP: {health}". That is clearer than gluing pieces together with +.

When this is useful
Use an f-string when the message has a fixed shape and the numbers or names inside it change.
concepts: A string is text in quotes
f-strings start with f before the opening quote
Expressions inside {} are evaluated and embedded
Prefer f-strings for formatted messages once you know the values' names

examples.title: Character status line
examples.explanation: Python substitutes the current values of name and health into the string.

examples.title: Forgot the leading f
examples.explanation: Without the f, braces print literally. The output is HP: {health}, not HP: 42.

examples.title: An expression in braces
examples.explanation: Braces can hold an expression, not only a single name. health + 10 is evaluated first.

common_mistakes: Forgetting the leading f — then {health} prints literally
Putting quotes incorrectly inside the braces

exercises.title: Predict the f-string
hints: Substitute the braced expressions with their values.
Keep the surrounding words and spaces exactly.
count becomes 3 and item becomes Potion inside one string.

exercises.title: Forgot the f
exercises.prompt:
This program is supposed to print:
Ready, Mira!

It currently prints the braces literally. Fix it.
hints: An f-string starts with f immediately before the quote.
The braces should contain the variable name, not extra quotes.
Turn the printed string into an f-string so {name} is replaced.

tests.message: Use an f-string that includes name inside braces — do not hardcode Mira.

exercises.title: Formatted character card
exercises.prompt:
The variables are already created. Print exactly one line:
Selene - Level 5 - HP 90

Use an f-string that inserts name, level, and health. Do not hardcode those values in the printed string.
exercises.starter_code:
name = "Selene"
health = 90
level = 5
# Print the formatted summary
hints: Start your string with f and put expressions in braces.
Keep the hyphens and spaces exactly as shown in the required line.
The printed f-string should mention name, level, and health inside braces.

tests.message: Use an f-string that includes name, level, and health in braces.
